title: Man dies in police custody; Victim arrested for public intoxication
article: Calgary police are investigating after a man was found dead in a cell in the arrest processing unit early Sunday.
Woodrow James Three Suns, 41, had been arrested on outstanding warrants and public intoxication around 7:35 p.m. Saturday at the Southland C-Train station.
He was arrested by LRT security, and transit police transported him to APU. Three Suns was checked by paramedics before he was booked into a cell, said duty inspector Barry Cochran.
Around 3:05 a.m., during one of the routine checks done by APU staff, Three Suns was found unresponsive on the floor of his cell.
Paramedics and unit staff tried to revive Three Suns before he was taken to hospital. He was pronounced dead on arrival, Cochran said.
Family members, who did not want to be identified, said Three Suns had medical issues which they believe caused his death.
"Mr. Woodrow James Three Suns was not a homeless person. In the Blackfoot way of life, we have a home for all our people," they said in a statement.
Three Suns had a young son, and an extended family on the Siksika Nation Reserve, they said.
An autopsy will be conducted this week.
The service's major crimes unit and the professional standards section are investigating.
Following the alcohol-poisoning death of Rahinder Johal while in police cells in 1999, the police service changed its policies, requiring APU staff to check inmates every 10 minutes.

Supervision at APU was a prominent issue during a 2001 fatality inquiry into the death of Willard Taypayosatum, 36, whose heart stopped as he lay unconscious in his cell. He had five times the legal limit of alcohol in his blood when he was found not breathing 21/2 hours after he was arrested for public intoxication on Dec. 10, 1998.
The paramedic on duty at the time testified he looked in on the three holding cells through one-way glass every 15 minutes.
